correctness.rationale: At fixed n>=3, k=n-2 and 0<=t<=n, a two-selected pair is either capacity-invalid or fails domination. A three-selected set must consist of an unmatched singleton on one shore and two matched vertices opposite: proved by an explicit omitted matched-partner obstruction and outside neighbor capacities. Counting these yields 2(n-t)C(t,2), only for 2<=t<n. All two-plus-two selected sets work, and endpoint cases exclude other size-four profiles. Direct independent adjacency enumeration n=3..8 for 39 graph profiles and 757248 subsets matches both exact minima and multiplicities.
